claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 15 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 15 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment by getting the first question.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is your child or the youngest child you're claiming for?**

To help me guide you through the eligibility assessment, I need to know:
- How old is the child? 
- Are they under 16, between 16-19, or 20 or older?

If you have multiple children of different ages, please start with the one you're inquiring about, and we can assess each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 15 years old, which means he falls into the "under 16" category. This is a good start for eligibility!

Let me proceed to the next check in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is important because children who work 24 or more hours per week have different eligibility rules. Please let me know Alex's current employment situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's still in school, so he's not doing any paid work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is not in paid work, that's a positive factor for eligibility. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, now I need to ask about any benefits Alex might be receiving:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

In other words, is Alex not claiming any of these benefits for himself? Please let me know.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 15-year-old living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive those benefits, which is good. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about Alex's apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in any apprenticeship?**

To clarify:
- Is Alex currently undertaking any type of apprenticeship programme? 
- If yes, which country/region is it in (England, Scotland, or Wales) and what type is it?

Since Alex is 15 and still in school, it's likely the answer is no, but please confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't started any apprenticeship. He's just doing his regular school work at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in any apprenticeship, so that's another positive factor. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. There are several possible paths to meet the residency requirements. Let me ask:

**Where do you normally live?**

Specifically:
- Do you normally live in the UK?
- Or, if not, do you have any of the following statuses:
  - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
  - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and if so, are you working, seeking work, studying, or have sufficient resources)?
  - Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

For most people, the answer will be that they normally live in the UK. Can you tell me about your residency situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirements. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm that you're responsible for Alex. "Responsibility" means one of the following:

**Which of these applies to you:**

1. **Do you live with Alex?** (This is the most common situation)

2. Or, if you don't live with him, are you:
   - Contributing to his upkeep (paying for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents)?
   - Paying maintenance under a court order or agreement?

Can you tell me which of these applies in your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, which clearly establishes your responsibility for him. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about any other potential claimants:

**Is there anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or anyone else who might also be claiming for him?**

In other words:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or guardian) also making a claim for Alex?

Please let me know if you're the only person claiming for Alex, or if there's someone else involved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only one claiming for Alex. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask about where Alex is currently living:

**Where does Alex normally live?**

Specifically:
- Is Alex living at home with you in the normal way?
- Or is Alex currently:
  - In hospital?
  - In care (such as a care home)?
  - Fostered with another family?

Please let me know about Alex's current living situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living at home with me - just a normal living situation. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you in a normal situation. Let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to ask one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the council paying for where Alex lives or contributing to his upkeep?
- Or are you fully responsible for paying for his accommodation and care?

Please let me know.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I'm fully responsible for all of Alex's accommodation and care costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You've passed all the eligibility checks. Let me confirm your eligibility and provide you with the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

**Great news!** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

---

### Summary of Your Eligibility

Alex meets all the requirements for Child Benefit:
- ✅ Age: 15 years old (under 16)
- ✅ Not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
- ✅ Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You live in the UK (residency requirement met)
- ✅ Alex lives with you (responsibility established)
- ✅ You're the only claimant
- ✅ Alex lives at home normally
- ✅ The council isn't paying towards his care

---

### Next Steps - How to Claim

To get your Child Benefit, you need to:

1. **Apply online** at: www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
   - Or apply by post using form CH2

2. **Prepare the following documents:**
   - Proof of your identity (e.g., passport, driving licence)
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - National Insurance numbers (yours and Alex's if available)

3. **Payment Details:**
   - Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)
   - Current Child Benefit rates are available on gov.uk

---

### Important Note - High Income Child Benefit Charge

If you or a partner earns over **£60,000 per year**, you may be subject to the High Income Child Benefit Charge. This means you may have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through self-assessment tax. More information is available at: www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-it-affects-other-benefits

---

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

All eligibility criteria have been met.
